title: Audit archive matrix and backfill casebook
body:
Executive summary:

This is a working note and decision matrix for how we map audit events to storage tiers, how we index for SIEM export and forensic queries, and the concrete backfill/reindex procedures for common failure modes. Goal: reduce ambiguous playbooks across infra, SRE, and secops by giving concrete examples, SLO targets, and step-by-step loops for backfills.

Context and scope:
- Covers user-visible audit events (auth, token creation, admin RBAC-v2 changes, policy changes, model serving decisions) and system-level pipeline events (ingest, transform, indexing).
- Includes retention defaults, archive windows, and when to escalate to e-discovery/legal.
- Notes on SIEM export throttling and field selection to keep exports compact.

Retention matrix (high-level):
- Hot tier (0-30 days): fast index, full-text, per-tenant primary shard. SLO: 99.9% query <200ms for recent 30d.
- Warm tier (31-365 days): columnar compressed indices, reduced replica count, headline fields indexed (timestamp, actor_id, action, resource, outcome). Slow queries allowed (SLO 95% <1s).
- Cold tier (1-7 years): object storage with compacted index manifests (file per day or per-week). Indexes are sparse: only event pointers and key metadata. Retrieval requires rehydration.
- E-Discovery / Legal hold: export snapshot to immutable object store with WORM flag, retained until legal clearance.

Mapping rules and examples:
- RBAC-v2 mutating events (role_create, role_update, permission_grant): keep full payload in hot tier for 90 days, warm 2 years, cold 7 years. Reason: forensic clarity when permissions change.
- Auth failures and suspicious login series: hot 180 days (enable alerting and retention extension if part of an investigation), warm 2 years, cold 3 years.
- System pipeline audits (transform errors, ingestion drop): hot 60 days, warm 1 year, cold 3 years. Backfill priority high because these indicate lost evidence.

Indexing and SIEM export strategy:
- Primary index fields (always indexed): timestamp, tenant_id, actor_id, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome, request_id.
- Secondary index fields (hot-tier only): full_message, request_headers, client_ip, user_agent.
- SIEM export payload should strip bulk fields: exclude request_headers and raw_request_body unless flagged. Provide a slimmed mapping to reduce export volume by ~40%.
- Export batching: hourly bundles with per-tenant chunking; max size per export 100MB to avoid SIEM ingestion throttles. Use gzip and newline-delimited JSON.

Backfill and reindex playbook (common scenarios):
1) Lost index shards after cluster upgrade (common, medium severity):
   - Detect: index_missing_shard alert + ingestion watermark gap.
   - Quick mitigation: pause indexing for affected tenant(s).
   - Backfill path A (if raw events available in cold OBJECT store): run rehydrate->transform->index job for date range; use parallelism=tenant_count but cap at 6 concurrent jobs to limit IO.
   - Backfill path B (if raw events partially lost): mark gaps in index and create placeholder tombstones with metadata documenting loss; notify security/legal.
   - Postmortem tags: JIRA link, summary, size of gap, root cause.

2) Corrupted transformation (schema drift) causing malformed documents in hot tier (high severity):
   - Detect: ingestion_error_rate > 0.5% + transform_error logs.
   - Hot rollback: revert transform to last-good image (artifact store) and reprocess in staging.
   - Safe reindex: run a schema-fix transform that emits compatibility fields; annotate reindexed docs with _reindex_run_id.

3) SIEM export duplication due to retry storms (low-medium severity):
   - Detect: SIEM-side duplicate ID counts or per-export checksums mismatches.
   - Mitigation: dedupe at export consumer using request_id + tenant_id; for immediate stop, pause export queue and purge pending retry metadata.

Failure modes and decision tree (short):
- Missing raw events in cold store -> escalate to SRE + legal if >1K events missing or >7 days span.
- Index backfill running > expected time -> reduce parallelism, increase retry backoff, check S3/EBS IO metrics.
- Unauthorized access detected in audit store -> freeze access keys, snapshot affected indices, start legal hold process.

Operational runbooks (step-by-step snippets):
- Rehydrate example CLI:
  ./tools/auditctl rehydrate --tenant $TENANT --from 2024-04-01 --to 2024-04-07 --parallel 4 --dry-run=false --tag reindex-apr-24
  Notes: run dry-run once to estimate output size. Rehydrate writes to staging-bucket/<tenant>/reindex/<tag>/

- Reindex job template (k8s):
  job_name: audit-reindex-{{tag}}-{{tenant}}
  env: SOURCE_BUCKET=staging-bucket/..., DEST_INDEX=audits-tenant-{{tenant}}-hot
  resources: cpu:2, mem:8Gi, ephemeral-storage:50Gi
  max_retries: 3

Monitoring and SLOs:
- Ingest SLI: percentage of events successfully indexed within 10 minutes of arrival; target 99.5% for hot tier.
- SIEM export SLI: percent of hourly exports delivered within 15 minutes of window close; target 99%.
- Backfill SLI: median reindex throughput >= 20K events/min per job for hot-tier reindexing (baseline on c5d-like nodes).

Queries and debug snippets (examples to paste into Kibana/ES):
- Find missing sequence in reindex set:
  GET audits-*/_search?q=tenant_id:%22$TENANT%22 AND _reindex_run_id:%22$TAG%22&size=0&aggs={"missing_seq":{"terms":{"field":"sequence_number","missing":true}}}

- SIEM export checksum validation (ps):
  cat export-2024-06-10.ndjson.gz | gunzip | md5sum

Open questions / proposals (to decide):
- Default warm retention: 1 year vs 2 years for non-admin events. Ops preference currently: 1 year to limit storage cost; sec prefers 2 years for investigations. Need final decision by July 1.
- Legal hold fast-path automation: propose an API that signals legal_hold:true on tenant, triggers snapshot to WORM and increments warm->e-discovery retention. Design doc: CONFLUENCE-SEC-1342.
- RBAC-v2 audit verbosity: should we record pre/post full role payloads for every permission_grant? Costly, but very helpful for forensics. Alternate: store diffs only.

Changelog (working):
- 2024-05-10 Priya: initial draft and matrix.
- 2024-05-22 Lina: added SIEM export batching caps and gzip guidance.
- 2024-06-12 Ethan: added reindex CLI examples and reindex SLI targets.

Appendix: quick checklist for incident lead (short):
- Identify time window and tenants affected.
- Check raw-object-store for presence of files (list with prefix date/tenant).
- If raw present: trigger rehydrate dry-run to estimate size.
- If missing: escalate and create placeholder tombstone index docs to record loss.
- Notify legal if >24h retention window breached or >10K events lost.

References:
- CONFLUENCE-SEC-1342: Legal hold automation proposal
- JIRA-AUDIT-922: Reindex job failures after 2024-05 cluster upgrade
- github.com/redwood-inference/audit-pipeline/pull/78: schema-fix for RBAC-v2 payloads

Notes to self:
- Coordinate with infra on EBS IO burst limits before running large reindexes.
- Add example Grafana dashboards: ingest-lag, reindex-throughput, siem-export-latency.

End of draft.
